I am an Assistant Professor in the Center for Biostatistics and Epidemiology within the Department of Biomedical Educations and Data Sciences at the Lewis Katz School of Medicine within Temple University. 
My day-to-day involves developing assisting trainees, residents and faculty with all statistical aspects of their projects, from IRB development and study design to statistical analyses and interpretation. 
In addition to the interdisciplinary, collaborative research with medical faculty, I continue to develop supervised dimension reduction methods for learning models by constructing summary statistics that describe the most endpoint-relevant features in the data.
My statistical methods development is motivated by electronic health records (EHRs), electrocardiogram (ECG) data and cardiovascular endpoints in renal disease patients. 


Prior to Temple, I was a Postdoctoral Researcher supervised by [Dr. Wensheng Guo](https://www.dbei.med.upenn.edu/bio/wensheng-guo-phd) and [Dr. Wei Yang](https://www.med.upenn.edu/apps/faculty/index.php/g275/p5888381) in the Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics (DBEI) at the Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania.
My research at Penn focused on developing methods to construct summary statistics that best describe features in the functional data that are most relevant to cardiovascular events. These methods were motivated and applied to the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study. 
Part of my duties as a postdoctoral researcher includes providing biostatistical support for clinical trials and cohort studies. 

I obtained my PhD in Statistics at [Penn State University](https://www.psu.edu/), under the supervision of [Dr. Bing Li](https://science.psu.edu/stat/people/bxl9), where I researched and developed sufficient dimension reduction methods for classification and functional data.
